top_signals.title: LayerZero says it ‘made a mistake’ in $292 Million Kelp exploit
top_signals.summary: LayerZero acknowledged a critical mistake that enabled a $292 million exploit of the Kelp protocol. The breach stemmed from LayerZero’s verifier being allowed to secure high‑value transfers in a vulnerable configuration, which the company now admits it “owns.” The incident raises serious concerns about the security of cross‑chain messaging infrastructure.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The LayerZero breach exposes systemic risk in cross‑chain messaging, likely compresses LayerZero valuations and forces VCs to prioritize bridge security audits before committing capital.

top_signals.title: Digital Asset Holdings Targets $300M in Latest Capital Raise
top_signals.summary: Digital Asset Holdings announced a target $300 million capital raise, underscoring growing investor confidence in tokenized finance. The article also highlights expanding enterprise adoption, with DTCC piloting tokenized assets, Moody’s publishing ratings on‑chain, JSCC testing on‑chain government bonds, and Swiss bank Amina supporting the Canton Coin.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Digital Asset’s $300 million raise confirms strong investor appetite for tokenization infrastructure and should lift valuations for platforms that can integrate with enterprise pipelines like DTCC.

top_signals.title: Customer Support & Dictation Loom Large As Voice Startup Leaders Prepare for a World of Talking Machines
top_signals.summary: Sierra announced a $950 million funding round at a $15.8 billion valuation, underscoring the rapid growth of voice‑AI startups. The summit also highlighted Wispr Flow’s fast‑growing dictation software and previewed OpenAI’s upcoming advanced voice models, signaling strong momentum in enterprise and consumer voice AI applications.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Sierra’s $950 million round at a $15.8 billion valuation signals massive capital flowing into voice‑AI, a layer that could become a key interface for on‑chain assistants and drive new use‑cases for Web3 applications.

top_signals.title: Prediction Market Kalshi Achieves $22B Valuation on Coatue-Led Series F Raise on Bankless
top_signals.summary: Kalshi, the U.S. prediction‑market platform, closed a $1 billion Series F round led by Coatue Management, lifting its valuation to $22 billion. The raise follows an 800% surge in institutional trading volume and positions Kalshi as the dominant player handling over 90% of U.S. prediction‑market activity.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Kalshi’s $22 billion valuation after a $1 billion Series F validates regulated prediction markets as a high‑growth vertical and positions it as a moat for future on‑chain betting platforms.

top_signals.title: KelpDAO/LayerZero Exploit Drains $290m, Freezes DeFi Markets
top_signals.summary: KelpDAO's liquid restaking token rsETH suffered a $290 million hack exploiting a LayerZero OFT bridge misconfiguration. The attacker used the stolen tokens as collateral on Aave, Compound and Euler to borrow $236 million, prompting market freezes and a $15 billion TVL decline across DeFi.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The KelpDAO/LayerZero exploit that froze DeFi markets underscores bridge fragility, prompting investors to demand stronger insurance and may depress overall DeFi valuations until security standards improve.

top_signals.title: Bullish’s Equiniti deal could remake it into a tokenization powerhouse, analysts say
top_signals.summary: Bullish announced a $4.2 billion acquisition of transfer‑agent Equiniti, a move analysts say will transform the firm into a tokenization infrastructure powerhouse. The deal gives Bullish direct access to issuer records and a regulated framework, positioning it to tokenise equities and compete in the emerging tokenized securities market.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Bullish’s $4.2 billion acquisition of Equiniti gives it a regulated transfer‑agent backbone, accelerating tokenized securities roll‑out and likely raises the multiple for tokenization infrastructure startups.

worth_a_read.note: LayerZero’s Cross‑Chain Messaging Crisis Multiple breaches this week exposed fundamental flaws in LayerZero’s verifier and OFT library, with a $292 million Kelp exploit and $3 billion of OFTs flagged as vulnerable. The incidents left roughly $178.5 million still at risk and sparked a mass migration away from the protocol. Implication: Investors and developers will prioritize platforms with immutable timelocks and audited multisig controls, accelerating capital shift toward more secure cross‑chain solutions.

Institutional Tokenization Gains Traction DTCC announced a forthcoming tokenization service for DTC‑custodied assets while Bullish’s $4.2 billion Equiniti acquisition gave it direct access to regulated issuer records. BlackRock filed paperwork for new on‑chain fund products and Digital Asset targeted a $300 million raise, underscoring deepening institutional confidence. Implication: Tokenized securities are moving from pilots to production, creating a sizable market for infrastructure providers that can bridge legacy custodial rails with blockchain.

AI Integration Becomes Core to Crypto Infrastructure Turnkey secured $12.5 million from Circle Ventures and Sequoia to launch a verifiable cloud platform aimed at AI‑driven digital‑asset workloads. At Consensus Miami, Trust Wallet and Mesh executives revealed wallet redesigns that enable AI agents to manage assets autonomously. Core Scientific’s $208 million Bitcoin sale funded an AI‑focused data‑center pivot, highlighting the convergence of AI compute and crypto mining. Implication: Infrastructure firms that embed AI capabilities into custody, computing and wallet layers will attract the next wave of venture capital and enterprise contracts.

Regulatory Clarity and Charter Pursuits Intensify The upcoming U.S. Clarity Act, highlighted at Consensus Miami, could be enacted as early as July 4, offering a comprehensive framework for digital assets. Kraken’s parent Payward filed for an OCC charter to become the first federally chartered crypto bank, while a U.S. judge cleared the way for Aave to move $71 million of frozen ETH. Binance faced a private compliance demand from the Treasury, signaling heightened enforcement pressure. Implication: Clearer rules and charter opportunities will reward compliant operators and may marginalize platforms that cannot meet federal standards.

DeFi Risk Management Overhauls After Kelp Collapse The Kelp DAO exploit triggered a $15 billion TVL drop across DeFi and forced Aave to seek an emergency hearing to release $71 million of frozen ETH. In response, Aave announced a comprehensive collateral standards revamp that adds cybersecurity and interoperability reviews. Implication: DeFi protocols are likely to adopt stricter risk‑assessment frameworks, creating demand for specialized audit services and risk‑monitoring tools that can certify compliance before new assets are onboarded.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, Another busy week for the crypto ecosystem and for Blockwall Capital’s radar. We reviewed 127 stories and three clear themes emerged: security stress, institutional momentum, and the rise of voice‑first AI in finance. First, the LayerZero incident reminded us why cross‑chain messaging remains a high‑risk surface. The company admitted a critical mistake that enabled a $292 million exploit of the Kelp protocol. A mis‑configured verifier on the OFT bridge let the attacker drain KelpDAO’s rsETH token, then reuse the stolen assets as collateral on Aave, Compound and Euler to borrow an additional $236 million. The fallout froze large segments of DeFi and contributed to a $15 billion drop in total TVL across the sector. This episode underscores the need for rigorous audit regimes and for investors to demand transparent post‑mortem processes. At the same time, institutional confidence is deepening. Digital Asset Holdings announced a $300 million capital raise, signalling strong appetite for tokenized finance infrastructure. The news dovetails with DTCC’s pilot of tokenized assets, Moody’s on‑chain ratings, and Swiss bank Amina’s support for the Canton Coin. On the prediction‑market side, Kalshi closed a $1 billion Series F round led by Coatue, lifting its valuation to $22 billion after an 800 percent surge in institutional trading volume. These moves are reflected in macro data: Bitcoin spot ETFs attracted $1.2 billion of net inflows this week, a rise of 18.5 percent, while total stablecoin supply climbed to $255.3 billion, up 2.1 percent. Finally, voice‑AI is breaking out of the consumer niche into enterprise finance. Sierra’s $950 million round at a $15.8 billion valuation highlights the speed of capital deployment in this space. Wispr Flow’s dictation platform is scaling rapidly and OpenAI’s upcoming voice models promise to reshape how traders and analysts interact with data. For European VCs, the convergence of voice‑AI and tokenized assets presents a fertile ground for co‑investment strategies. Looking ahead, the market will test whether security upgrades can restore confidence in DeFi bridges while institutional pipelines continue to swell. How will you position your portfolio to balance these opportunities and risks in the coming week? #Web3 #Crypto #Blockchain #CryptoVC #WeeklyDigest
